chapter: Riverboat to New Orleans and Horace Henderson
title: Tommy Amagon's Villa gives the stranded band beds and a grill
summary: A jazz-loving club owner let them play weekends for the take and put beds in the hall; Luke Stewart earned tips at a hotel to buy groceries, and Granger grew desperate to go home.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: It was a pretty well known family in Buffalo.
And he had a place called the Villa, out by the old railroad station in Buffalo, and he liked jazz musicians. In those days you ran into a lot of people that

just liked jazz musicians. They'd sit and listen all night, and they couldn't play nothing but they'd be right there, you know. Every time there was a jam session they'd stay there as long as the musicians would.

So he had a place, he said, "Well, come on and play. Play for me on --," so he saw us jamming. We didn't worry about it. We had no place to stay, had nothing, you know, and no way to get no food, but we'd be at a jam session that night, you know. So what happened, he said, "I tell you what you do. You come on out there on Saturday and Sunday and play for me," you know, and he said, "Whatever I take in just split it up between you, you know." So we said good. So we went out there and we did that, and he said, "Look, I'll tell you what I'm going to do for you guys. I'm going to put some beds in here." He had a place on the side of the hall. Said, "I'll put some beds in here for you guys."

Said, "I'm going to put some beds in here for you, and I'm going to --," said, "Now, you can get your food, if you can hustle up enough money to buy some food, then you can cook it right here on the grill." He had the grill where he cooked his hamburgers and hot dogs, you know?
Well I'll be darned. Fancy that. He was

Never forgot him for that either. But it was great. Now we had a guitar player. This guitar player I'm telling you about, Luke Stewart, he would go out, he had a little more experience than we did, because he didn't come up in that band. He come up with the other guys. So he knew a little bit more about getting around. So he would go to a hotel called the Vendome Hotel, which was in the black neighborhood, in the Harlem part of Buffalo, and he'd go in there and play for tips. And he would come back and he would get the tips, and the tips was good there, and he'd buy a whole lot of groceries and stuff, and he'd bring them out there and we'd cook them, you know, and things like that. So we made it like that for a couple of weeks. Then Granger said, "Oh, I can't do this. I've got to get away from here, you know." I said, "Well, heck, let's don't be in a hurry. Let's try and see if we can get something. Don't run right back home. Let's see what can happen out here, you know."
